[MUQATIL:10:31-35/r1] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | Rain and crops, hearing and sight, life from semen and death from the living, and governance belong to God; Quraysh acknowledge this, so they should abandon shirk and fear punishment.
[AKHFASH:v1p373/r4] AKHFASH, d. 215 · author | holds | أم can precede من because من is not inherently interrogative but stands in place of the interrogative alif; أم supplies an indispensable meaning.
[AKHFASH:v1p373/r5] AKHFASH, d. 215 · author | holds | The same explanation allows an interrogative particle to precede هل; interrogation originally belongs to the alif.
[AKHFASH:v1p373/r6] AKHFASH, d. 215 · الشاعر | reports | A poem's هل ... أم هل construction illustrates أم following هل.
[TAB-FULL:v12p175#2/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | God controls hearing and sight, can strengthen or take them away, brings the living from the dead and the dead from the living, and governs all affairs; the audience admits He does this, so they are asked why they do not fear His punishment and abandon shirk.
[TAB-FULL:v12p175#2/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | God governs the affairs of the heavens, earth, all within them, and human beings; the people answer that God does all this.
[ZAJJAJ:v3p16#2/r9] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | The questions about provision, hearing, sight, life, death, and governance establish God’s oneness because only God can do these things; the audience answers ‘God.’
[IBNABIHATIM:v6p1950/r1] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · مجاهد | reports | God alone decides and carries out the affair.
[IBNABIHATIM:v6p1950/r2] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · الضحاك | reports | Fearing God means guarding against Hell through the five daily prayers.
[IBNABIHATIM:v6p1950/r3] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · مجاهد | reports | An alternative gloss reads the question as asking whether they are able to fear God.
[SULAMI:v1p301#3/r1] SULAMI, d. 412 · قيل | reports | The question about God's management of affairs points to the changing turns of the cosmos.
[SULAMI:v1p301#3/r2] SULAMI, d. 412 · الواسطي | reports | God initiates and renews affairs through time and manages them; this leaves no basis for claiming independent agency through one's own acts and work.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r1] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | As God alone creates, He alone provides sustenance.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r10] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | Truth is a divine name: God exists, possesses truth, and makes truth actual; for creatures, truth is good action, sound belief, and permissible speech.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r12] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | Conjecture favors one judgment without certainty; it is defective regarding God, while certainty about one’s own future is also defective.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r13] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | A servant should not presume to know his own unseen future, but should have certainty about God; the Prophet and his followers are told to call with insight. | mentions 12:108
[QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r14] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | The heedless grow blinder the more they hear the Qur’an, while people of spiritual realization grow in guidance; God’s address confuses some and enlightens others.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r2] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | Bodily provision is obedience granted to some and failures granted to others; spiritual provision is connection for some, heedlessness and later punishment or respite for others.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r3] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | For the spirits, provision means realities of intimacy for some, but worldly heedlessness and eventual punishment or respite for others.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r4] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | God’s control of hearing and sight means He perfects some people’s vision through monotheism and blinds others to realization.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r5] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | Bringing the living from the dead and the dead from the living means bringing a believer from an unbeliever and an unbeliever from a believer.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r6] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | Although they answer God, they speak from conjecture and words without inward conviction.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r7] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | All created things and events are subject to divine will, decree, and power; the decree has already passed and cannot be altered.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r8] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | Causes cannot alter what is eternal or reverse God’s decree.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p14/r9] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | He rejects both assigning partners in creation under the doctrine of predestination and denying God’s power to resurrect; both are unbelief.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p186/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس؛ المفسرون | reports | The one who provides from sky and earth sends rain and brings out plants.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p186/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | Owning hearing and sight means creating them for people.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p186/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | Bringing the living from the dead includes believer from disbeliever, plant from earth, human from sperm, bird from egg, stalk from grain, and palm from seed, with the reverse process likewise.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p186/r4] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | God directs the affairs of this world and the next; the audience admits He does these things, so they are challenged to fear Him and abandon partners.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:30-31/r2] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | God sends rain and grows plants, created hearing and sight, and brings believers from disbelievers, plants from earth, and people from semen, as well as their opposites.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:30-31/r3] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | God directs the affairs of this world and the next; since people admit He does these things, they should fear Him and associate nothing with Him.
[JISHUMI:v5p3361/r1] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | God brings worshippers together with idols, then separates the parties, who disavow one another; idols are also brought to life.
[JISHUMI:v5p3361/r2] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Everyone receives the consequence of good or evil; no manufactured deity can help, harm, avert punishment, or independently intercede with God.
[JISHUMI:v5p3361/r3] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Worshipping idols and fabricating claims are human acts, for which people are punished and reproached, against the Compulsionists' account of human acts.
[JISHUMI:v5p3361/r5] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Rizq is an ongoing gift or benefit its recipient may use and others may not withhold; only God is called the Provider because He creates provision, like the exclusive title Lord despite ordinary possessive uses.
[JISHUMI:v5p3362/r1] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | The questions establish God's unity and resurrection: God sends rain and produces plants, or sends clouds, rain, celestial bodies, and vegetation, as al-Aṣamm explains.
[JISHUMI:v5p3362/r2] JISHUMI, d. 494 · أبو مسلم | reports | God owns hearing and sight by creating and arranging these faculties, granting or taking them away, or enabling people to hear admonition and see lessons.
[JISHUMI:v5p3362/r3] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | reports | Bringing the living from the dead may mean a human from a drop and a drop from a human, or giving and taking life; God's management includes day and night, seasons, people, life, and death.
[JISHUMI:v5p3362/r4] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | The polytheists will acknowledge that God performs these acts, so they should fear His punishment and worship no other.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p132/r1] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | God provides rain from the sky and plants from the earth, grants hearing and sight, brings living things from dead matter and dead matter from living things, and governs events.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p132/r2] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | He brings a living being from a sperm-drop and the sperm-drop from a living being.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p132/r3] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | The Arabs acknowledge that God performs these acts; they are therefore asked why they do not fear His punishment for associating partners with Him, or why they still commit shirk despite that acknowledgment.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p328#2/r1] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | God provides from heaven and earth, pouring out His favors and widening His mercy.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p328#2/r2] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | reports | ‘Who owns hearing and sight?’ asks who creates and fashions them remarkably, or who protects these delicate organs from many hazards.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p328#2/r3] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | Managing affairs means directing the whole world, stated generally after specific examples.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p328#2/r4] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | ‘Will you not fear?’ means protect yourselves from punishment for your misguidance.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p117#2/r1] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The questions are a rebuke and proof with no escape: God provides rain from heaven and growth from earth, owns hearing and sight, brings life from death and death from life, and governs all affairs.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p117#2/r2] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Examples of bringing the living from the dead include an embryo from semen, bird from egg, and growing plant from earth; the reverse includes egg from bird, while divine governance proceeds through complete, eternal knowledge rather than thought or change.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p117#2/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | They have no answer but God; once they admit His power, the rebuke asks why they do not fear Him instead of treating idols as gods.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p28/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | God provides rain from heaven and plants from earth; He created hearing and sight and brings the living from the dead and the dead from the living, as previously discussed at 3:27. | mentions 3:27

597 · author | holds | God directs the affairs of this world and the next; the audience admits it is God because only He can do these things, proving His oneness.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p28/r3] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbas interprets “will you not be mindful?” as “will you not take warning?”
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p28/r4] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · مقاتل | reports | Muqatil reads the question as “will you not fear associating partners with God?”
[RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | After exposing idol worship, the author argues from provision, senses, life and death, and God's governance against associating partners with Him.
[RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Provision depends on rain from the sky and nourishment from the earth; plants originate in earth and animal diets must ultimately reach plants, since an endless chain of animals eating animals is impossible.
[RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Since only God governs the heavens and earth, He alone provides; hearing and sight are the noblest senses.
[RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · علي | reports | ʿAlī is quoted praising the Creator who gives sight through fat, hearing through bone, and speech through flesh.
[RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | The living from the dead and dead from the living may mean humans and birds from sperm and eggs and vice versa, or believers from unbelievers and vice versa; most favor the first, closer to the literal sense.
[RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r6] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The general statement that God directs affairs summarizes limitless governance in the upper and lower worlds and in the worlds of spirits and bodies.
[RAZI-FULL:v17p70#2/r7] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The Meccan polytheists acknowledged God as provider and governor but claimed idols brought them near or interceded, despite knowing idols neither benefit nor harm; they should fear assigning them worship.
[QURTUBI-FULL:10:31/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The passage rebuts polytheists and establishes the proof: if they acknowledge God's acts, the case is clear; if not, any rational person must recognize that the heavens and earth have a creator, a truth close to immediate necessity.
[QURTUBI-FULL:10:31/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Provision from heaven is rain and provision from earth is vegetation.
[QURTUBI-FULL:10:31/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | God owns hearing and sight because He made and created them for people.
[QURTUBI-FULL:10:31/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Examples of bringing the living from the dead include vegetation from earth, a person from a sperm drop, an ear of grain from a seed, a bird from an egg, and a believer from a disbeliever.
[QURTUBI-FULL:10:31/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Managing the affair means determining and carrying it out.
[QURTUBI-FULL:10:31/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The polytheists will answer “God,” since they believe He is the Creator; alternatively, an honest and thoughtful person will reach this answer.
[QURTUBI-FULL:10:31/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The concluding question urges them to fear God's punishment and retribution in this life and the next.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:10:31/r1] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Provision from heaven and earth comes from both, from each broadly, or from their inhabitants with an omitted noun.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:10:31/r2] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Owning hearing and sight means creating and shaping them or protecting them from frequent, easily triggered harm.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:10:31/r3] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Bringing living from dead means giving life and death, or creating animals from sperm and sperm from animals.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:10:31/r4] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Managing the world generalizes after the specific powers; people will answer God because the proof is too clear to deny.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:10:31/r5] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | They should fear God's punishment rather than associate partners who share none of His powers.
[NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#3/r1] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | God provides from heaven through rain and from earth through vegetation.
[NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#3/r2] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | reports | God alone creates and forms hearing and sight in their astonishing detail, or protects their delicate organs from injury over time.
[NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#3/r3] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | reports | Bringing the living from the dead and the dead from the living can mean animals, chicks, crops, believers, and scholars from fluids, eggs, and seeds, and their opposites.
[NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#3/r4] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | Management of the whole world follows the particular examples, widening the argument from specific divine powers to universal governance.
[NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#3/r5] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | Since they acknowledge God as the only one able to do these things, they should abandon associating partners with Him in worship.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p51#2/r10] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhsharī explains God’s control as creating the senses in their remarkable form or protecting them from pervasive injury; Abū Ḥayyān says these nuances do not follow from the wording.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p51#2/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | After exposing idol worship, God confronts them with undeniable evidence: provision, hearing and sight, life and death, and governance of all things.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p51#2/r8] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Provision essential to life comes from rain in the sky and vegetation on earth; min marks its source and indicates generosity from both upper and lower worlds.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p51#2/r9] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Hearing and sight are the two noblest senses: hearing enables perception, sight surveys creation, and God controls their preservation or removal.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · علي | reports | ʿAlī praises God as one who gives sight through fat, hearing through bone, and speech through flesh.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Here am signals transition to another proof rather than abrogating the prior question with bal; it cannot be treated as bal without the interrogative hamza.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Hearing and sight stand for the senses generally because they are most distinguished; creating living from dead and dead from living displays God’s power to bring opposites from one another.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The universal statement that God governs all things follows four examples because His governance has no limit; the unbelievers cannot deny that God provides, controls, creates life and death, and governs.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | “Will you not be mindful?” warns them to fear punishment for inventing partners for God; alternatively it asks them to take warning and stop.
[SAMIN-DURR:10:31/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | من السماء may mark origin, part, or kind; the partitive and kind readings require an omitted أهل.
[SAMIN-DURR:10:31/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | أم is disconnected because no interrogative hamza or equivalence preceded it; here it means بل alone since an explicit interrogative من follows. | mentions 27:84
[SAMIN-DURR:10:31/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | The transition is a transfer to a new point, not cancellation of what came before, following the Qur'anic pattern.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p266#2/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | Rainwater makes crops grow by God's power, as illustrated by the listed produce; the question about who provides it invokes 80:27–31 and 67:21 to establish His exclusive lordship. | mentions 80:27, 80:28, 80:29, 80:30, 80:31, 67:21
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p266#2/r2] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | God gave people hearing and sight and could take them away; Ibn Kathīr links this to 67:23 and 6:46. | mentions 67:23, 6:46
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p266#3/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | Bringing the living from the dead and the dead from the living occurs by God's immense power and grace; the verse is general and includes all the interpretations previously discussed.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p266#3/r2] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | God alone governs all creation and none can overturn His judgment; every heavenly and earthly creature depends on Him, as in 55:29. | mentions 55:29
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p266#3/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | Since the polytheists admit God does all this, they should fear Him instead of worshiping others through opinion and ignorance.
[BURHAN:v2p471/r1] BURHAN, d. 794 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhsharī groups “who manages the affair” after “who provides for you” with the preceding category of coordinated expressions.
[BURHAN:v2p471/r2] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | Coordinating synonyms or near-synonyms with واو adds emphasis; it occurs in clauses and especially in word pairs with different wording. | mentions 3:146, 20:112, 20:77, 74:22, 12:86, 74:28, 4:171, 20:107, 43:80, 5:48, 17:52, 33:67, 33:12, 35:35
[BIQAI-FULL:v3p438/r5] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The questions about provision, senses, life, death, and universal governance expose what the polytheists already admit, thereby proving God’s exclusive divinity and rebuking their denial of resurrection.
[BIQAI-FULL:v3p438/r6] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | God provides rain and other benefits from the sky, and plants and other means of life from the earth.
